extracted.intended_audience: eligible hospitals and critical access hospitals (CAHs), health IT developers, hospital compliance officers, and stakeholders in the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed changes to CMS requirements for the Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program, including revisions to the CEHRT definition, removal of attestations, and removal or revision of specific measures and supporting ONC certification criteria that hospitals and CAHs must use to demonstrate meaningful use of certified EHR technology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Certified Electronic Health Record Technology (CEHRT) (42 CFR 495.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: For 2019 and subsequent years CEHRT requires EHR technology certified under the ONC Health IT Certification Program that meets the 2015 Edition Base EHR definition (or subsequent Base EHR) and is certified to specified ONC health IT certification criteria in 45 CFR 170.315. The definition further specifies particular criteria (e.g., family health history 170.315(a)(12), patient health information capture 170.315(e)(3)) and that EHR technology be certified to criteria necessary to be a Meaningful EHR User, including applicable measure calculation certification criteria (170.315(g)(1) or (g)(2)) and clinical quality measure certification criteria (170.315(c)(2), (c)(3)(i) and (ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes revising the CEHRT definition to remove references to 170.315(a)(12), 170.315(e)(3), 170.315(g)(1), and 170.315(g)(2) effective January 1, 2027, arguing that functionality is widely embedded and developers will continue to support it even if separate certification criteria are removed, and that removing these references reduces administrative burden without impacting reporting requirements. The proposed revised regulatory text and rationale are provided; public comment is invited.

rubrics_metrics.name: ONC HTI-5 Proposed Updates to ONC Health IT Certification Program
rubrics_metrics.description: ONC's HTI-5 proposed rule identified many certification criteria for removal (34) and revision (7) across 45 CFR 170.315 and seeks to reduce developer burden, offer flexibility, and support innovation by removing or revising certain certification criteria and provisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS summarizes the HTI-5 proposals and their potential impact on Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program participants (see tables referenced). If ONC finalizes removals/revisions, corresponding CEHRT references in 42 CFR 495.4 would be adjusted; CMS notes it may finalize related changes irrespective of ONC action. Stakeholders should review HTI-5 proposed rule details (90 FR 60970) for specific criteria affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: ONC Direct Review attestation (current requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible hospitals and CAHs must affirm cooperation with ONC Direct Review of their CEHRT by acknowledging the requirement to cooperate in good faith and, if requested, cooperating in good faith with ONC direct review. Currently a 'Yes' response (or claiming an exclusion) is required; a 'No' causes failure to meet the attestation and failure to be a meaningful EHR user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes to remove this required attestation beginning with the EHR reporting period in CY 2026 (data submission period beginning Jan 1, 2027), arguing the attestation is no longer necessary because ONC direct review processes are known and the value of participation is evident without an annual attestation. CMS encourages continued cooperation with ONC direct review when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: ONC-Authorized Certification Body (ONC-ACB) Surveillance attestation (current optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: An optional attestation that eligible hospitals and CAHs may indicate they acknowledge the option to cooperate and, if requested, cooperated in good faith with ONC-ACB surveillance of their certified health IT. Currently optional answers ('Yes', 'No', or non-response) do not affect meaningful EHR user status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes to remove this optional attestation beginning with the EHR reporting period in CY 2026 (data submission period Jan 1, 2027) to reduce reporting burden, while strongly encouraging continued participation in surveillance activities when requested by ONC or ONC-ACBs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support Electronic Referral Loops by Sending Health Information measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires, for at least one transition of care or referral, that the eligible hospital or CAH (1) creates a summary of care record using CEHRT and (2) electronically exchanges the summary of care record.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerator: number of transitions/referrals where a summary was created using CEHRT and exchanged electronically. Denominator: number of transitions/referrals during the EHR reporting period where the facility was the transitioning or referring provider (POS 21 or 23). This measure historically relied on the 'transitions of care' certification criterion (45 CFR 170.315(b)(1)). CMS proposes removal of this measure beginning with the EHR reporting period in CY 2028; the rule explains the measure's history and rationale for removal (shift toward network-based exchange and FHIR adoption).

rubrics_metrics.name: Support Electronic Referral Loops by Receiving and Reconciling Health Information measure
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires, for at least one electronic summary of care record received using CEHRT (either as recipient of a transition/referral or first-encounter patient), that the eligible hospital or CAH conducts clinical information reconciliation for medication, medication allergy, and current problem list using CEHRT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numerator: number of electronic summaries received for which reconciliation of the three clinical information sets is completed using CEHRT. Denominator: number of electronic summaries received using CEHRT for which the facility was the reconciling party, and for first-time patients. The measure uses the 'transitions of care' (170.315(b)(1)) and 'clinical information reconciliation and incorporation' (170.315(b)(2)) certification criteria. CMS proposes removal of this measure beginning with the EHR reporting period in CY 2028, with rationale focusing on program streamlining and encouraging newer exchange modalities (e.g., FHIR and network-based exchange).

rubrics_metrics.name: Health Information Exchange objective reporting options and scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Under current policy, eligible hospitals and CAHs must satisfy the Health Information Exchange objective by using one of three reporting options: Option 1 (report both Sending and Receiving Referral Loop measures), Option 2 (report HIE Bi-Directional Exchange), or Option 3 (report Enabling Exchange Under TEFCA). The Sending and Receiving Referral Loop measures are each worth 15 points (max 30 points). Beginning with the EHR reporting period in CY 2027, facilities must attest 'Yes' on the Electronic Prior Authorization measure to meet all requirements for the objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes removing the two Referral Loop measures beginning in CY 2028 so the objective would be satisfied by attesting 'Yes' to either HIE Bi-Directional Exchange or Enabling Exchange Under TEFCA, and by attesting 'Yes' or claiming an Exclusion on Electronic Prior Authorization. CMS provides program data showing reporting trends (e.g., higher reporting of HIE Bi-Directional than Referral Loop measures) and invites comment on barriers for small/rural hospitals and CAHs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification criteria supporting Referral Loop measures (45 CFR 170.315(b)(1) and (b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'transitions of care' criterion at 170.315(b)(1) supports creation and exchange of summary of care records (C-CDA-based), and the 'clinical information reconciliation and incorporation' criterion at 170.315(b)(2) supports reconciliation on receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ONC's HTI-5 proposed rule would reduce the scope of 170.315(b)(1) to focus on receipt of C-CDA documents and position the criterion toward future receipt of FHIR-formatted data, and would remove 170.315(b)(2) based on industry adoption. CMS explains these criteria enable the actions required by the measures and notes ONC's review found broad implementation of these capabilities even if certification criteria are removed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Health Registry Reporting measure and supporting certification criterion (170.315(f)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: ONC proposed removing the only certification criterion (170.315(f)(7) — 'transmission to public health agencies — health care surveys') that supports the Public Health Registry Reporting measure. If removed, there would be no specific certification criteria identified for this measure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS explains that eligible hospitals/CAHs could use any available data exchange standard specified in 45 CFR part 170 subpart B to meet the measure (e.g., C-CDA per 170.205(a)(4) or QRDA per 170.205(h)(2)). CMS discusses the impact and references HTI-5 proposals for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Case Reporting and Antimicrobial Surveillance measures and supporting criteria (170.315(f)(5) and (f)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: ONC proposed revisions to 170.315(f)(5) (electronic case reporting) and 170.315(f)(6) (antimicrobial use/resistance reporting) to update certification criteria to focus on functional rather than standards-based requirements. These criteria are identified as supporting the corresponding Medicare Promoting Interoperability Program measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS notes that while ONC's proposals would revise certification requirements for health IT products certified to these criteria, eligible hospitals and CAHs would continue to need to use health IT certified to these criteria to report the Electronic Case Reporting, Antimicrobial Use Surveillance, and Antimicrobial Resistance Surveillance measures if the criteria remain in effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other certification criteria removals/revisions with program implications (examples: 170.315(a)(14), 170.315(h)(1),(h)(2), 170.315(a)(5), 170.315(b)(11), 170.315(g)(3),(g)(4), privacy/security series)
rubrics_metrics.description: ONC proposed removing or revising a range of certification criteria referenced in CEHRT or Base EHR definitions (examples cited include implantable device list 170.315(a)(14), transport methods 170.315(h)(1) and (h)(2), patient demographics 170.315(a)(5), decision support interventions 170.315(b)(11), safety-enhanced design 170.315(g)(3), quality management system 170.315(g)(4), and a series of privacy/security capabilities in 170.315(d)(1)-(13)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS explains that removal of such criteria from ONC's program would remove the regulatory requirement that an eligible hospital/CAH must use CEHRT that includes the functionality, but notes that removal of criteria does not change obligations under other laws (e.g., HIPAA) to ensure privacy and security. CMS points readers to Table IX.F-07 and HTI-5 for a complete listing and impact analysis; stakeholders should consider developer and provider burden, continued availability of functionality, and patient safety implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and implementation of proposed changes
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS proposes specific implementation dates for the various changes: removal of certain CEHRT certification criteria effective January 1, 2027; removal of ONC Direct Review and ONC-ACB Surveillance attestations beginning with the EHR reporting period in CY 2026 (data submission period opening Jan 1, 2027); and removal of the Support Electronic Referral Loops by Sending and Receiving measures beginning with the EHR reporting period in CY 2028.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS provides rationale for these timelines (minimize burden, feasibility for hospitals and CMS to implement changes prior to submission deadlines) and notes there would be no effect on FY 2028 payment determinations or FY 2026 cost reimbursement if attestations are removed as proposed. Public comment is invited on timing and substance.
